reference.source: Resnick's Diagnosis of Bone and Joint Disorders / GeneReviews
clinicalPearls: Radiographic hallmark is fine longitudinal linear striations in the metaphyses of long bones and the iliac wings, combined with dense sclerosis of the skull base and cranial vault
Caused by variants in AMER1 (also called WTX) on the X chromosome, which regulates WNT/beta-catenin signalling and bone formation

X-linked inheritance produces a striking sex difference: affected females have a relatively mild phenotype, whereas affected males are severely affected and the condition may be lethal in males in some families
Cranial sclerosis can narrow neural foramina and cause cranial-nerve deficits, notably hearing loss and facial palsy
Characteristic facial features include macrocephaly, frontal bossing, hypertelorism and a flat nasal bridge
The linear metaphyseal striations are asymptomatic and do not weaken the bone, in contrast to the clinically important skull-base thickening
Management centres on hearing surveillance and decompression of narrowed cranial-nerve foramina where progressive deficits arise, alongside multidisciplinary supportive care
reference.pathophysiology: Osteopathia striata with cranial sclerosis results from loss-of-function variants in AMER1 (WTX), an X-linked gene whose protein modulates the WNT/beta-catenin pathway that governs osteoblast differentiation and bone mass. Dysregulated WNT signalling produces two contrasting bony patterns: benign linear striations within the metaphyses of tubular bones and the pelvis, and progressive sclerotic thickening of the cranial vault and skull base. Because the gene lies on the X chromosome, hemizygous males typically show a severe or prenatally lethal phenotype, while heterozygous females, protected by X-inactivation mosaicism, display milder disease. The skull-base overgrowth encroaches on foramina, accounting for the cranial neuropathies.
additionalDifferentials: Osteopoikilosis and other sclerosing bone dysplasias
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey demonstrating metaphyseal striations and iliac involvement
Skull radiographs or CT showing cranial vault and skull-base sclerosis and foraminal narrowing
Audiometry to detect and monitor conductive or sensorineural hearing loss
Cranial-nerve examination and neuroimaging when deficits develop
AMER1 molecular genetic testing and X-linked family segregation analysis
Developmental and cardiac evaluation in severely affected males where indicated
redFlags: Progressive hearing loss or facial weakness indicating cranial-nerve foraminal compression
Visual disturbance suggesting optic canal narrowing
Severe presentation in a male fetus or neonate, which may be life-threatening
Raised intracranial features or airway compromise from extensive craniofacial overgrowth
reference.prognosis: Affected females generally have a good prognosis with intellect usually preserved, though cranial-nerve complications may accrue over time; affected males can have severe multisystem disease that is frequently lethal in the prenatal or neonatal period.
pitfalls: Mistaking the benign metaphyseal striations for a sinister process and overlooking the clinically important cranial sclerosis
Failing to recognise the X-linked inheritance and the marked male severity when counselling families
Delaying audiological and cranial-nerve surveillance until deficits are advanced
Attributing developmental or facial features to an unrelated syndrome without genetic confirmation
references: Resnick's Diagnosis of Bone and Joint Disorders
management: No disease-modifying drug exists, so management targets the cranial-nerve complications of skull-base sclerosis with structured surveillance
Serial audiometry and hearing rehabilitation with amplification for conductive or sensorineural loss from foraminal narrowing
Cranial-nerve monitoring and neuroimaging when facial palsy, hearing loss or other deficits develop, with surgical foraminal decompression for progressive compression
Multidisciplinary craniofacial input for macrocephaly, cleft palate repair and associated dysmorphism
AMER1 molecular confirmation and clinical genetics referral with X-linked family segregation counselling
Antenatal and paediatric evaluation of hemizygous males, who may have severe or lethal multisystem disease
